# dsh-window-size-keeper
English | 中文
Keeps the DSH desktop window the size you left it: host half + a settings-page section, zero externa
esktop window the size you left it: host half + a settings-page section, zero external dependencies.
> Changelog: CHANGELOG.md (English) / CHANGELOG.zh-CN.md (Simplified Chinese) — the two are maintain

ed together.
> The release ledger (`RELEASES.txt`), the publish/submission guide (`PUBLISHING.md`) a
nd the market submission entry (`submission/`) live only in this checkout (they are not part of the
published package) — see "What lives where on a machine" at the end.
## The problem
DSH desktop (Electron) rebuilds its main window at a fixed default size (1280×820) on every start, s
o the size you resized to last time is lost. This plugin records the main window's last **outer fram
e** (title bar and borders included, in physical pixels), restores and centres it on the next start,
and adds a **Window size** section to the DSH settings page where you can pick 1920×1080, 1280×720
and other common resolutions, or any custom width×height.
## The “Window size” settings section (added 2026-10-11)
DSH desktop → Settings → **Window size** (the same level as the Plugins and Desk pet sections, `orde
r: 65`). What's in it:
| Control | What it does |

| Restore size radio group | "Last size" (default) / 12 common resolutions / "Custom…" |
| Custom wi

dth & height inputs | any size (outer frame, physical pixels) via "Apply custom size" |
| Centre on

restore switch | centres on the primary work area; off = resize only, position untouched |
| Apply c

urrent selection | re-runs one resize with the current selection, changing nothing |
| Current outer
frame / next-start size / file paths | status read-out |
**When it takes effect:** immediately — picking a value resizes the main window at once (centring pe
r your setting) and writes it to the settings file, so the next start uses the same size.
About the numbers: every value is the **outer frame** (title bar + borders) in **physical pixels**,
identical to what `GetWindowRect` returns. With DPI scaling above 100% the same numbers look smaller
than they read (1920×1080 does not fit a 1920-wide screen at 125% scaling and gets clamped to the w
ork area), which is why the list includes `1536×864` (= 1920×1080 at 125% scaling).
## Display language (added 2026-10-19)
All copy in this section is translated; the language is resolved in this order:
| # | Source | Behaviour |
| 1 | `language` in patch config (delivered to the page through `GET /state`) | `"zh"` / `"en"` pins
the language. Anything unrecognised — including `zh-TW` — is not treated as "pinned Chinese" and fa

lls through |
| 2 | The DSH client's active language (`ctx.locale`, i.e. Settings → General → Langua
ge) | follows whatever you selected in DSH, **switching languages takes effect at once** — no reload
, no restart, and no rebuild of the section (text already typed into the custom width/height boxes s

urvives the switch) |
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
- The host process (DSH host, a child of the Electron main process) **starts watching the main windo
w at `apply` time**: it keeps a resident Win32 agent - first choice a small helper exe compiled on t
he user's own machine, `powershell.exe` as fallback - that enumerates windows every 40 ms and acts t
he moment the main window appears. Identification rule: host parent PID + `Chrome_WidgetWin_1` windo
w class + outer-frame area ≥ `earlyMinArea`. While watching, the window is still **hidden** and its
title has not become the product name yet, so this stage identifies windows by area (which keeps the
600×700 welcome window and the 720×760 login window out); when two candidates have similar areas it

declares "can't tell" and looks again next round — it never guesses.
- **Why that yields "opens at
last time's size":** the desktop app creates its main window **hidden → `loadURL` → `show()`** (`cre
ateWindow(appPreload, false, true)` and `enterWorkspace` in `lib/main.js`), and Electron only create
s it after the host reports `ready`. So there is a window of time where the main window exists but i
sn't visible, and the agent finishes resizing inside it — the window's very first appearance is alre
ady the target size, so the boot animation no longer plays at the wrong resolution. If nothing is fo

und (or `restoreEarly: false`), the plugin falls back to the old `restoreDelayMs` polling path.
- Ta
rget size priority: **settings-page selection (`settings.json`) > `preset` in patch config > "last s
ize" (`state.json`)**. Restores via Win32 `SetWindowPos`, centring on the primary work area (`center
OnRestore`, on by default; off = size only), clamped to `[minW,minH]` and to the current work area (
a window bigger than the work area is pinned to the top-left). Occasional `SetWindowPos`/Win32 failu
res retry up to 3 times (1 s apart); if all fail, the actual size is persisted and retried on next s

tart (self-healing).
[该节后续省略]

## What lives where on a machine
`<workspace>/dsh-window-size-keeper` is the one checkout: code, both READMEs, both changelogs, the r
elease ledger, `PUBLISHING.md`, the market submission entry, CI and `.git`. Version identity is the
annotated tag `v<version>` - the old habit of keeping a second directory named `<name>-<version>` as
a release snapshot was retired on 2026-10-20 and nothing depends on it. `<workspace>` stands for "w
herever this checkout lives on your machine" — the repo deliberately records no absolute paths from
anyone's machine, and a selftest group enforces that. What DSH actually runs is a packaged artifact
rather than this directory: `npm pack` writes `dist/<name>-<version>.tgz` and the profile installs i
t from `~/.dsh/.plugin-sources/<name>-<version>.tgz`, so editing `lib/*.js` here takes effect only a
fter pack + `dsh plugin … add` + a full DSH restart (or a temporary `link:` while debugging). Everyt
hing the plugin writes at runtime lives in `~/.dsh/storages/window-size-keeper/`: `state.json`, `set
tings.json`, `state.json.gen`, plus the compiled `wsk-agent-*.exe` and its `.cs` (deleting those onl
y means recompiling next time, and deleting `state.json` restarts the "last size" history).
